locator.panel: loss of CH3*, product printed third (lower right): [C3H7C(C2H5)=OH]+ m/z 101, 10%

evidence.curator_note: Book draws 2 arc(s) for this pathway; moves <1,2> are drawn, move <3> is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page). ARC COUNT, verified by zooming the scan: FOUR arcs are printed on the one structure - one SOLID fishhook from the odd electron drawn as '+.' on the hydroxyl oxygen, ending with a half-arrowhead (barb) on the C-O bond, and THREE DASHED fishhooks, one from each alpha C-C bond, all ending with a barb on that same C-O bond. This record takes the two arcs of the C-CH3 channel: the shared solid oxygen hook (move 1) and the dashed arc that descends from the vertical C(1)-CH3 bond to the barb sitting above the C-O bond (move 2). The electron that departs with the methyl radical is NOT drawn. LOCALIZATION (convention B): the charge and the odd electron are drawn on oxygen, and the precursor SMILES writes that literally as [OH+:8] with two bonds and one unpaired electron. Methyl loss is the slowest of the three competing alpha cleavages, 10% versus 50% (C2H5* loss) and 100% (C3H7* loss); the corresponding m/z 101 peak in Figure 4.2 is drawn as a very small peak labelled '101 alpha', noticeably weaker than a tenth of the base peak, so the printed 10% should be read as the book's rounded relative rate rather than a measurement read off that figure.

Cross-linked MOD rule variable: IMS_4_17_3 '[C]1([C]2[C]3[C]4)([C]5[C]6)([C]7)([O+.]8)>>[C]2[C]3[C]4[C]1([C]5[C]6)[O+.]8.[C]7'. VERIFIED, not asserted. (i) Left side is the same tertiary-carbinol pattern as the other 4.17 variants and matches this record's precursor exactly: RDKit substructure test of the equivalent SMARTS [#6]([#6][#6][#6])([#6][#6])([#6])[O+] returns True with a single match mapping the rule's 2-4/5-6/7/8 onto propyl/ethyl/methyl/oxygen. The product retains propyl and ethyl on C1 and expels C7, so this is the methyl-loss, m/z 101 channel. (ii) Right side is MIS-ENCODED relative to the book exactly as its two siblings are: the oxygen remains [O+.]8 SINGLY bonded to C1, so the C=O(+) pi bond the arrows form is never created and the odd electron is left on oxygen, and the leaving methyl is written [C]7 instead of [C.]7. The ion's formula and m/z are right (C6H13O, +1, m/z 101) but it is emitted as an odd-electron species with a three-coordinate unlabelled carbinol carbon rather than the drawn even-electron oxocarbenium [C3H7C(C2H5)=OH]+. The conservation guardrail passes it because atoms, total charge (+1 -> +1) and total unpaired count (1 -> 1) are numerically unchanged. Re-authoring all three as '...[C]1{=}[O+]8 . [C.]x' would make them faithful to the equation.
